title: Key rotation & exit data-handling scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal notes to prepare negotiating positions and redline snippets for customers asking about key custody, rotation, and exit handling on Private/Dedicated deployments. Focus: what we can accept, hard no's, fallbacks, and suggested draft language for contracts and SOWs.

Summary takeaways (toplines for negotiation):
- Prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for customers with strict compliance. If BYOK accepted, require clear operational boundaries and a minimum set of provider logs/metrics for support.
- If provider-managed KMS/HSM: insist on attestations (FIPS/HSM cert), documented rotation windows, and limited copy/backups of KEKs.
- Do not accept unrestricted key escrow with single-party control. If escrow is required, insist on multi-party escrow (split-key / quorum) and documented ceremony.
- Exit must include: a) final data export, b) proof of deletion, c) key handover or key destroy confirmation. Timeline: aim for 30 days for export and key handover; escalate to 60 days max with fees.

Clauses to flag in counterpart drafts:
- "Customer keys" definition vagueness: ensure distinction between data-encryption keys (DEK), key-encryption keys (KEK), and signing keys. We should not hold customer signing keys unless explicit.
- Broad indemnities tied to key compromise: push back; cap liability and require mutual negligence bar.
- Rights to persist copies/backups: limit to disaster recovery with retention window and delete-after-policy.
- Audit/access to logs: customer needs proof of actions (key import/rotation/backup events) but not raw key material.
- Cross-border transfer language: ensure crypto material and exports comply with both parties' residency needs.

Negotiation asks: tiered approach (what we ask for, what we can concede)
- Ask (MVP): BYOK with HSM provider attestations, weekly rotation allowed by customer, provider limited to metadata only, provider to maintain operation logs for support.
- Concede (if customer pushes): Provider-managed KMS with written rotation schedule and HSM attestation, customer gets cryptographically-verifiable export and key-destroy proof on termination.
- Last-resort (avoid): Provider escrow of KEK under provider-only control. Only accepted with multi-sig escrow and defined ceremony + independent auditor.

Operational checklist for legal & sales to confirm before signature:
- Is the deployment Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated? (Private -> BYOK expected; Dedicated -> negotiation heavier)
- Will customer provide KMS/HSM credentials or request Redwood-managed?
- Required compliance certifications (SOC2, FedRAMP, PCI, HIPAA) that drive key control needs?
- Backup/disaster recovery policy: can provider retain encrypted backups containing DEKs? For how long?
- Test rotation runbook: can we run a simulated rotation before go-live?

Suggested redline snippets (draft language):
- Customer-Managed Keys (preferred):
  "Customer shall have the option to supply and control Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) used for encrypting data at rest (\"Customer Keys\"). Provider shall never export, copy, or persist Customer Keys in plaintext. Provider shall maintain logs of key use (key ID, timestamp, operation) and make those logs available to Customer upon request for audits. Provider may not use Customer Keys for any purpose other than performing the Services under this Agreement."

- Provider-Managed Keys (fallback):
  "If Customer elects Provider-managed keys, Provider shall use an HSM that meets FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (or later) and shall provide attestation of HSM configuration upon request. Provider shall rotate KEKs according to the schedule in Exhibit A; Customer shall receive cryptographic proof of rotation and a snapshot of key fingerprints. Prior to termination, Provider shall provide a secure export of DEKs or a documented key-destruction confirmation per Section X."

- Key Handover & Exit:
  "Upon termination or expiration, Provider shall, within thirty (30) days, export Customer data in the format specified by Customer and either hand over Customer Keys (if applicable) via a mutually agreed secure channel or provide verifiable destruction evidence of Customer Keys. If Customer requests key handover and Provider holds KEKs, the parties shall perform a key handover ceremony (Exhibit B) with a minimum of two authorized representatives present. If mutually agreed, an independent third-party may observe to verify proper handover or destruction."

- Audit & Proof Language (deletions/handovers):
  "Provider shall provide Customer with: (a) a signed statement including a hash of the exported dataset, (b) key fingerprints of any handed-over keys, and (c) a deletion certificate signed by Provider’s security officer confirming permanent removal of key material from live systems and backups according to the retention schedule in Exhibit C."

Operational runbook notes (engineering-friendly):
- Test case: staging rotate with test KEK every 90 days, validate token issuance with rotated keys, verify ability to decrypt legacy ciphertext. Document steps and time to rollback.
- Backup verification: ensure backups include key metadata only (fingerprints) and not raw KEK/DEK material.
- For BYOK flows: automate import API with strict idempotency, revoke old keys on rotation with time-windowed re-encryption plan.

Edge-case questions to resolve with Legal/Infra:
- Can we accept an SLA that includes key-rotation downtime windows? If customer demands continuous availability, require overlap-window for rotations.
- How to handle legal requests (subpoenas) for keys when customer-managed? Default to ask customer, but need process for emergency legal disclosure.
- Are we comfortable performing key-ceremony with customer on-prem agents during exit? Operational burden? SOW estimate needed.

Points for Legal to draft / follow-up items:
- Draft Exhibit A: rotation schedule + evidence artifacts (what cryptographic proofs look like).
- Draft Exhibit B: key-ceremony checklist (who signs, what logs are captured, timeframe).
- SOW language for termination assistance and hourly caps for on-site/remote key handover work.

Negotiation scripts / quick talking points for AE/SE:
- "BYOK gives you control and reduces our surface area — we can support it and log operations for you. If BYOK isn’t possible, we use HSM with attestations and provide verifiable proofs at exit."
- "We do not keep plaintext keys. If you need escrow, we can agree a split-key escrow with a neutral custodian — this is more secure but will add time and cost to the rollout."
- "For termination we aim for 30 days to export and handover; if you need faster turnaround we can include it in the SOW for an extra fee."

Redlines I'm planning to propose in the upcoming deal (notes to self):
- Add explicit definitions for KEK/DEK/signing keys in the Definitions section.
- Add 30-day export + deletion certificate clause.
- Replace any "unlimited retention or backups" phrasing with explicit retention windows and destruction obligations.
- Require HSM attestation if provider-managed or require BYOK otherwise.

Open risks / watchlist:
- Customer may insist on provider-only escrow with no third-party — hard no unless legal & security approve with SOW and extra controls.
- If customer requires unredacted forensic logs, we need narrow scoping — provide only event-level logs, not key material.
- International export controls: must check sanctions and crypto export restrictions for customer region before promising cross-border key movement.

Quick links / references for tech/legal teams:
- Proposed Exhibit templates (placeholder): CONF-4532
- Key import/export API docs: JIRA-INFRA-987
- Slack thread with infra patterns: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/keys-team/p123456

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. Convert into a short playbook and an Exhibit A/B draft for Legal before next GTM call. Track any exceptions in the deal log.

--- end scratchpad ---
